sections.h2: What to line up before listing in Westlake
sections.html:
Westlake lies in Cuyahoga County roughly 12 miles west of downtown Cleveland. An estimated 33,904 people live here, 1.0% fewer than in 2020. City Hall sits at 27700 Hilliard Boulevard, phone 440-871-3300, open 8 am to 4 pm.

For permits and property maintenance, ask City Hall directly. For deeds and value complaints, use the Cuyahoga County Fiscal Office and Board of Revision. The sections below explain what each office does.

sections.h2: Housing costs and who lives here
sections.html:
Westlake is an older suburb where most households own.

  • Owners live in 73.1% of homes, valued at $368,200 at the midpoint.
  • Monthly housing costs are $2,071 with a mortgage and $926 without.
  • Typical rent is $1,570.
  • 14,424 households share the city, averaging 2.29 people.
  • The middle household income is $112,200.
  • Residents 65 or older make up 25.1%, and median age is 47.4.

Given those ages, expect many Westlake sales to involve downsizing owners or heirs settling an estate. Of 15,508 housing units in 2020, 5.7% were vacant. Owner-occupied houses rarely sat empty (0.8%), while rentals did more often (8.5%).

Dover Village took the name Westlake in 1940 and became a city in 1957. Population jumped from 12,906 in 1960 to 27,018 in 1990 and 34,228 in 2020, which means a lot of the housing dates to the postwar decades.

Crocker Park, a mixed-use center built around a small-town street plan, holds 1,050,000 square feet of retail, 650 residential units and 100,000 square feet of office space. Workers here commute 24.4 minutes on average, a fact to mention to downtown commuters.

sections.h2: Deed transfer at the Cuyahoga County Fiscal Office
sections.html:
No city office touches a Westlake deed. Filing happens with the county Fiscal Office, whose Transfer and Recording division took over from the old auditor, recorder and engineer. Call 216-443-2060 with questions.

  • Every transfer needs a state form, either the DTE 100 value statement and receipt or the DTE 100-EX, which explains why no conveyance fee is due.
  • County staff won't write your deed, since that counts as legal work. Use a title company or attorney.
Where to go for common Westlake sale tasks
TaskOfficeWhat to know
Permits, building and property maintenance questionsCity of Westlake Building Department, through City Hall at 440-871-3300City Hall hours are 8 am to 4 pm
Deed transfer and recordingCuyahoga County Fiscal Office, 216-443-2060DTE 100 or DTE 100-EX accompanies each transfer
Value complaintCuyahoga County Board of Revision, 216-443-7195Complaint window opens January 1 and ends March 31

Valuation complaints go to the county's Board of Revision under Chapter 5715 of the Revised Code. For tax year 2026 you can file from January 1 through March 31, 2027. The statute sets the deadline at the end of March following the tax year, unless first-half collection closes later.

You'll find the board upstairs at 2079 East Ninth Street (second floor). Phone 216-443-7195 or email BORInfo@cuyahogacounty.gov. Its site posts the state forms, a searchable list of closed and pending complaints since 2018 and guidance on evidence. Ohio Revised Code 5715.19 requires a complainant to give the board all information or evidence they hold that affects the property.

Read the evidence guidance on the board's site before you file. A complainant who withholds evidence can be barred from using it on appeal.

In 2020 Westlake had 14,618 households. About half (49.4%) were married couples, 35.3% were one person, and 16.3% were someone 65 or older living alone. Just 22.8% included children under 18. Plenty of buyers may want low upkeep, so a tidy house with simple systems can appeal.

At a typical value of $368,200, most buyers will borrow, and their lender sets the pace. An as-is direct buyer can close when you want, though the offer will reflect the work the house needs.

  • Insist on written offers that name the closing date, who pays closing costs and what repairs are carved out.
  • Request proof of funds from a cash buyer before anything else.
  • Compare what's left after the mortgage payoff and unpaid property tax, because the headline price overstates what you keep.

Work backward from the day you want to close. Clear permit and complaint questions with City Hall first, so the title company finds nothing unexpected. Book your deed preparer next. Last, weigh offers by what you'd net, and get cost splits in writing.

A value dispute can only be filed between January 1 and March 31, so a fall sale shouldn't wait on one. The Board of Revision decides value, and your closing doesn't depend on its ruling.

When an offer arrives, read it for three things: the closing date, the costs assigned to you, and any repair the buyer wants fixed. A cash buyer who accepts the house as-is should say so in writing. Keep copies of the signed disclosure form and any permit paperwork in one folder, because the title company, the buyer and the county may each ask for a piece of it. If heirs are involved, make sure everyone who must sign the deed is lined up before you accept a closing date.

sections.h2: Questions to ask City Hall before listing
sections.html:
Skip the guesswork and put these questions to City Hall.

  • Does any permit remain open or lack a final inspection?
  • For a rental: is a license or registration required, and does it pass to the buyer?
  • Any open maintenance or zoning complaints?
  • Which sewer and water accounts need a final reading on closing day?
  • Is the signed state disclosure form ready? Under section 5302.30 sellers of one-to-four unit homes must deliver it, except in estate sales and some family transfers.

Write down each answer with the date and department. Your title company will probably ask the same things.

Once you have answers, work through the county side. Have a title company or attorney draft the deed, choose the DTE form, and check Fiscal Office requirements ahead of closing. A cash buyer can skip the lender's appraisal, but not these local and county steps. Ask the title company to confirm that each sewer and water account has a final reading on the closing date, and keep a dated note of every call to the city so the paperwork trail is easy to hand over.

faqs.q: By when must a Westlake value complaint be filed?
faqs.a: The end of March following the tax year. For tax year 2026 the Board of Revision lists January 1 through March 31, 2027. Call 216-443-7195 with questions.

faqs.q: Who prepares the deed for a Westlake sale?
faqs.a: A title company or attorney does. Fiscal Office staff can't draft deeds because the county treats that as legal work. Each transfer goes with a DTE 100 or DTE 100-EX.

faqs.q: Where do I call about Westlake permits and property maintenance?
faqs.a: City Hall at 440-871-3300, open 8 am to 4 pm. Ask about any open permit that never got a final inspection and any open maintenance or zoning complaint.

faqs.q: What does Westlake's disclosure form cover?
faqs.a: Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 makes sellers of one-to-four unit homes deliver the state form to the buyer. Estates and some family transfers are exempt.

faqs.q: How should I compare a cash offer with a listing?
faqs.a: Get each offer in writing with the closing date, who pays closing costs and any repair exclusions. Ask a cash buyer for proof of funds, and compare what you'd keep after paying off a mortgage and unpaid property tax.
